newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iran dismisses allegation of link to Saudi bombing.
newsitem.headline: Iran dismisses allegation of link to Saudi bombing.

text.p: Iran's U.N. mission on Monday dismissed as fiction and propaganda newspaper allegations that its officials were behind the bombing of a U.S. military compound in Saudi Arabia last year.

It said an article in Sunday's Washington Post and other papers was in line with the "customary practice of certain Western quarters to exploit any situation to feed the public their not-so-hidden-anymore agenda of anti-Iran propapaganda."

"The article in question and other media reports on the issue are permeated with conjectures, fiction stories and pure allegations," a statement from the mission said, adding that Iran rejected such allegations as "biased, unfounded and pure fabrication."

The Post story, attributed to unnamed U.S. and Arab officials, linked a senior Iranian government official to a group of Shiite Moslems suspected of bombing a U.S. military compound in Saudi Arabia last year.

It said Brig. Ahmad Sherifi, a senior Iranian intelligence officer, met two years before the bombing with Hani Abd Rahim Sayegh, a Saudi Shiite arrested in Canada last month as "a direct participant" in the June 25 blast that killed 19 U.S. servicemen.
